spans.s:
aryá, a. faithful; attached, kindly, 79^3.
[‘going eagerly to,’ √ṛ: cf. ā́rya.]

ā́rya, a. belonging to the faithful, i. e., as
m., man of one's own tribe, an Aryan, as
designation of a man of the Vedic Indian
tribes; as adj. Aryan; noble; reverend
(used in respectful address). [aryá, 1208f:
cf. Avestan airya, ‘Aryan’; New Persian,
īrān, ‘Persia’; Hdt. vii. 62, οἱ Μῆδοι ἐκα-
[]
λέοντο πάλαι Ἄριοι; Keltic nom. eriu, acc.
erinn, name of Ireland; Eng. Ir-ish: cf.
arí, aryá.]

aryamán [426a], m. bosom-friend, esp. a
bridegroom's friend, παρανύμφιος; Aryaman,
 name of an Aditya (invoked at the
wedding, and often with play upon the
appellative mg of the word). [aryá.]
